also for the clues, VRChat could make a optional choice and rely by default on english language, but if a user sets a language tag, like (English, Japanese or Italian)
it could help the speech-to-text to process captions as well.

Spatial.io has this feature I think, I haven't tried it (since everyone I sign with is on VRChat), but I think this would be a super neat feature and since spatial.io has it implemented, it shows that it's already something that's happening in competing platforms.
I am Deaf person, and I agree with you. When they start talk, subtitle/closed caption will show up, it'll be helpful. Emmvrc also have this Closed Caption Mod as well.
People should look into this: https://www.patreon.com/RabidCrab no mods needed, runs with EAC just fine
Venompapa: its nice but not everyone can pay for it. also its for a user to convert *their own* speech to text but it doesnt convert other users speech into text like CC mod

@{60c669b16f356233845a9198|full_name}: Here is a free option you can try https://github.com/VRCWizard/TTS-Voice-Wizard (if you want to convert other peoples voices you have to get a virtual cable that takes audio from vrchat and put it as the input device for the app. If you are interested in trying it, join the Discord linked on the Github and I can help you out.

author.name: Scout - VRChat Head of Quality Assurance

comments.value: I legitimately need this so bad, I struggle with hearing and a lot if times when I'm in large crowds, I have a harder time communicating with others which ends up leaving me feeling isolated :(

details:
I am in deaf communities. Often I have noticed hearing (speaking) people join, and then try to learn sign language but end up using their voices to communicate. While it's difficult to understand if they keep getting frustrated and going back to use their voices, I would like to suggest this feature for the general public use so we can work together and get over the language barrier and help each other to learn how to sign and communicate with each other. It would be useful if it has the options to disable/enable if you don't need to use them or want to use them just in case somebody approaches a deaf person and try to talk to them verbally in public worlds. That'd be swell. Optional feature: subtitles appear over their heads and the words are facing at you so you can read them while they talk to you if that works.

EDIT: Second Optional feature: If you're an RPG player and you prefer this, have the subtitles show up on your HUD instead of above their heads. it'll look like this;
Name1: *text*
Name2: *text*
(April 7, 2021)

Second Edit: (10/21/2021)
Made some edits on grammar errors and such.
I also have an interesting suggestion; One day I found out the headset has a pointer-click (invisible computer mouse if you will) in the exact center of the HUD. That made me think of this new idea: Possible Optional, you look at the person, and the subtitles will focus on that person and transcribe what they are saying, ignoring the rest of the people around you (if you don't like the background chatter) so I think that'd be a neat idea.
title: Speech to Text feature for deaf/hard of hearing people
